(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_001, SEVERITY: 0.88, FLAW_CLASS: 5, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.63, DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` only iterates over `responses.items()` for failure detection. Any active model that was allocated work but returns no `ModelResponse` entry is not passed through `FailureHandler.detect_failure()`, does not accrue a transport failure, and is not considered in recovery except indirectly via a later health-monitor heuristic. This breaks Area 6’s stated contract of typed failure handling for dispatch outcomes: a silent non-response is the strongest failure case but is currently invisible to the primary failure pipeline. As a result, a missing PM response may not trigger PM-specific retry/abort policy, and missing PAR/COL responses remain active with no failure history update. PROPOSED_FIX: In `process_round()`, iterate over the expected/active dispatched model set, not just `responses`. Synthesize an explicit missing-response failure (or map it to `EMPTY`/`TIMEOUT` per contract) for any dispatched model absent from `responses`, then pass it through the normal `detect_failure`/`get_recovery` path. VERIFIED: FALSE)

(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_002, SEVERITY: 0.79, FLAW_CLASS: 2, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.56, DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` determines repetition using `same_type_count >= self.config.n_fail` before recording the current failure. This means escalation occurs on the `(n_fail + 1)`-th occurrence, not the `n_fail`-th. The built-in `validate_k1()` comments confirm this off-by-one behavior (“Third call would be repeated”), which is inconsistent with the usual reading of “after n_fail failures, escalate” and makes the threshold semantics misleading. PROPOSED_FIX: Define the policy explicitly and align implementation with it. If escalation is intended on the `n_fail`-th observed failure, compute repetition as `(same_type_count + 1) >= self.config.n_fail`, or record first then evaluate against history including the current event. Update validator comments/docs to match. VERIFIED: FALSE)

(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_003, SEVERITY: 0.72, FLAW_CLASS: 1, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.60, DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` appends to `_perf_history` only when execution reaches the UNDERPERFORM branch, i.e. after the response has already passed EMPTY/TIMEOUT/MALFORMED/FORMAT checks. Therefore rounds with transport/protocol failures are omitted from performance history entirely. This biases the persistence-window underperformance detector toward optimism: a model can alternate between malformed/timeout rounds and weak-valid rounds without the bad rounds contributing to the persistence window, delaying or preventing downgrade. PROPOSED_FIX: Decide whether non-valid responses should count as worst-case performance for persistence purposes. If yes, record a sentinel performance value (e.g. 0.0) for all failed responses before early return. If no, document that underperformance history excludes transport/protocol failures and justify the separation. VERIFIED: FALSE)

(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_004, SEVERITY: 0.67, FLAW_CLASS: 2, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.51, DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.__init__()` stores `self.role_map = role_map` by reference rather than copying it. Because `DynamicManager` later mutates `self.failure_handler.role_map = self.role_assignment.role_map`, and callers could also mutate the original dict externally, failure classification for PM/non-PM recovery depends on aliasing external mutable state. This makes recovery outcomes time-dependent in a non-local way and complicates auditability of failure decisions. PROPOSED_FIX: Copy the role map on ingestion (`dict(role_map)`) and provide an explicit setter/update method that replaces it atomically when reassignment occurs. If historical audit matters, consider versioning role maps by round. VERIFIED: FALSE)

(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_005, SEVERITY: 0.64, FLAW_CLASS: 4, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58, DESCRIPTION: `DynamicManager.process_round()` records boolean failure history into `RoleAssignment` only for models present in `responses`. Models absent from `responses` receive no `record_failure(..., False)` or `record_failure(..., True)` update. Since reassignment penalties are driven by this history, a model that repeatedly disappears can avoid both the FailureHandler’s typed history and RoleAssignment’s failure-rate penalty, remaining artificially attractive for future rounds. This is distinct from the missing-response detection bug because it also corrupts cross-area adaptation state even when other logic notices the absence elsewhere. PROPOSED_FIX: Update failure history for every expected/dispatched model each round. Missing response should be recorded as failure in both Area 6 and Area 1 penalty history. VERIFIED: FALSE)

(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_006, SEVERITY: 0.57, FLAW_CLASS: 8, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.47, DESCRIPTION: `detect_failure()` emits an event for FORMAT violations using `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` rather than a format-specific event type. This collapses two distinct failure categories in the real-time monitoring interface, making downstream telemetry, dashboards, and automated handlers unable to distinguish parse failures from formatting noncompliance. The returned `FailureType` is correct, but the event stream loses information. PROPOSED_FIX: Add and use a dedicated `ManagerEventType.FORMAT` (or a general failure event with failure subtype in metadata) when `response.format_compliant` is false. VERIFIED: FALSE)

(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_007, SEVERITY: 0.55, FLAW_CLASS: 1, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.66, DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.should_abort()` applies `return len(self._active_models) < self.config.k_min` even though its own docstring says “If only PM survives, framework degrades to single-model mode.” Unless `k_min` is guaranteed to be 1, these statements conflict: with `k_min > 1`, a surviving PM-only state aborts rather than degrades. This is a policy inconsistency between the coded stop condition and the documented reduction behavior. PROPOSED_FIX: Make the intended invariant explicit. Either set/validate `k_min == 1` when PM-only degradation is supported, or change the docstring and reduction validators to state that falling below `k_min` always aborts, including PM-only cases. VERIFIED: FALSE)

(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_008, SEVERITY: 0.48, FLAW_CLASS: 6, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.44, DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler` accepts `role_map` and model universe independently but does not validate that every role-mapped model exists in `models` and vice versa. Recovery logic, PM detection, and abort checks then operate over potentially divergent sets, with unknown PM IDs or orphaned active models yielding silent fallback behavior (`_expected_performance` returns 0.0, role defaults to `PAR`, pm lookup may point outside `self.models`). PROPOSED_FIX: Validate in `__init__()` that `set(role_map.keys()) == {m.model_id for m in models}` or, if partial maps are intended, document and enforce the exact allowed subset relation with explicit errors on unknown IDs. VERIFIED: FALSE)

(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_009, SEVERITY: 0.43, FLAW_CLASS: 2, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.41, DESCRIPTION: `check_reallocation_depth()` / `record_reallocation()` maintain `_realloc_depth` monotonically per `task_id` with no reset mechanism by round or by successful completion. If task IDs are reused across rounds, previously accumulated depth will permanently block future reallocations for unrelated later rounds. The docstring frames this as a cascade guard for a task’s current reallocation chain, not lifetime process state. PROPOSED_FIX: Scope reallocation depth by `(round_idx, task_id)` or clear depths at the start/end of each round. If task IDs are globally unique by contract, document that invariant explicitly. VERIFIED: FALSE)

(FINDING_ID: R6_FH_010, SEVERITY: 0.34, FLAW_CLASS: 8, ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.35, DESCRIPTION: `FailureHandler.get_recovery()` documents “PM failure with transport/protocol type after retry -> ABORT (HARD)” but only treats `EMPTY`, `TIMEOUT`, and `MALFORMED` as PM-abort-eligible. `FORMAT` is excluded and falls through to standard policy (`DEGRADE`/`RETRY_CLARIFIED`), despite also being a protocol/interface failure in the surrounding taxonomy. This may be intentional, but the contract language is ambiguous and materially affects PM safety policy. PROPOSED_FIX: Clarify whether FORMAT is considered protocol failure for PM handling. If yes, include it in the PM hard-failure set; if no, narrow the docstring to name the exact failure types. VERIFIED: FALSE)

[VERIFY:current] Cross-component concern from this scope only: the manager’s failure pipeline appears to assume the orchestrator will always provide a `responses` entry for every dispatched model. If another component’s contract says missing entries are allowed to represent silent failures, R6_FH_001 and R6_FH_005 become high-confidence true integration defects; if not, they remain API-contract weaknesses that should still be defended against.
